goal: Allow a future mixed owner-teacher corpus to preserve each case's original source authorization and source-specific rights issuer, without forging one synthetic authorization over AMI public teaching evidence.
procedure: Keep the existing synthetic v1 manifest frozen. A separate v2 intake and manifest declare an externally authenticated umbrella authorization reference and exhaustive per-(case authorization ID, source family) bindings to exact source-rights authority references and issuer IDs. Admission checks each case's original authorization against the registered binding and each source receipt's authority/issuer against that binding, rejects a reused source ID under a conflicting authorization, and rejects unused bindings. The assembler checks the same before producing a separate v2 manifest; no mixed manifest has yet been assembled.
decision_criteria: v2 manifest and intake schemas distinct from v1
umbrella authorization supplied and authenticated outside checker
every (original authorization ID, source family) binding used once and points to exact rights authority/issuer
source ID cannot switch authorization between cases
training and distribution rights for train or evaluation rights for diagnostic development still required
authority: Read MFM local 92a606b code and focused tests as a structural admission method. It does not issue an umbrella authorization, authenticate the underlying AMI copyright/noncopyright assertions, place the blocked private archive in persistent custody, assemble a mixed corpus or process it on Magnolia.
validation: Compared v2 admission and assembler code fields to the FBM seed; JSON parse and local diff checks only. The integrated MFM branch is published at ae7d680286b84a5755caeb1d2e82e0d09c5176ae.
failure_or_lesson: A combined manifest must bind original case authority and source-rights issuer instead of changing an existing case ID or authorization string to satisfy a single-ID checker. Structural hash matching is narrower than authentic authorization.
